name: Augustiner-Museum Rattenberg
kurzbeschreibung: The Augustiner-Museum in Rattenberg: top-class museum of sacred art in the 1385 Gothic Augustinian monastery with accessible church tower.
beschreibung:
Overview

The renowned Augustiner-Museum is situated in the picturesque glass town of Rattenberg – Austria's smallest town – in the Tyrolean Unterinntal (Kufstein district) at an altitude of 521 meters. Housed within the venerable walls of the former Augustiner-Eremiten-Kloster, founded in 1385, it is regarded as one of the most significant and awarded specialized museums for Christian art in western Austria. Opened in 1993, the museum was honored with the Austrian Museum Prize and the prestigious Europa Nostra Diploma, preserving an invaluable collection of Gothic and Baroque sacred art treasures from across Tyrol.

Monastery Architecture & Sacred Treasures

The monastery complex itself is an architectural masterpiece of Late Gothic and Baroque architecture: visitors can tour the atmospheric cloister, the Gothic monastery church, and the Baroque sacristy with its elaborate marquetry. The collection spans outstanding masterpieces from nine centuries of religious life: highlights include magnificent Late Gothic sculptures and winged altarpieces by renowned masters such as Michael Pacher and his workshop, exquisite goldsmith works, Baroque monstrances, precious liturgical vestments, processional banners, and richly colored paintings by artists like Franz Anton Zeiller. An architectural highlight for visitors is ascending the accessible church tower: a historic wooden staircase leads to the belfry and onward to the open viewing platform of the tower, providing spectacular views over the historic gables and roofs of the old town of Rattenberg, the Inn River, and the Schlossberg ruins.

Visit & Getting There

The Augustiner-Museum Rattenberg is open during the season from May to the end of October, Tuesday through Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (closed on Mondays). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €8.00, seniors approx. €7.00, and children and youth under 18 enjoy free admission! With the regional Alpbachtal Card, admission is free. Getting there by public transport: take the train (ÖBB/S-Bahn) to Rattenberg-Kramsach station, from where it is just a three-minute walk through the historic town gate into the town center. By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Kramsach/Alpbachtal), park in the large visitor parking lots P1 to P3 on the outskirts of Rattenberg (Rattenberg itself is a completely car-free pedestrian zone).

Tips

The ground floor of the museum, including the cloister and monastery church, is barrier-free and wheelchair accessible; ascending the historic tower requires climbing stairs. Combine your museum visit with a stroll through the glassblowing workshops of Rattenberg and taste authentic Tyrolean apple strudel in the traditional pastry shops along Südtiroler Straße.
